name: Brazil Nut Effect (Cereal Box Effect)
description: The tendency of larger particles to rise to the top of a shaken mixture while smaller particles settle into the spaces below.

name: Busy Beaver Function
description: A function measuring the maximum work done by a halting Turing machine of a given size, growing faster than any computable function.

name: Multi-Armed Bandit Problem
description: A sequential decision problem about balancing exploration of uncertain options with exploitation of the best option found so far.

name: Pancake Sorting
description: The problem of sorting a stack using only prefix reversals, as if flipping the top portion with a spatula.

name: Cheerios Effect
description: The attraction or repulsion of small floating objects caused by gravity and the curved liquid surfaces around them.

name: Fridge Light Fallacy
description: The mistake of assuming a state is always present because checking for it creates or reveals it, like a refrigerator light turning on when the door opens.

name: Buttered cat paradox
description: A humorous thought experiment combining the claims that cats land on their feet and buttered toast lands butter-side down.

name: Sad clown paradox
description: The apparent contradiction between making others laugh and privately experiencing depression, anxiety, or emotional distress.

name: When a white horse is not a horse
description: A classical Chinese argument that explores how a qualified category such as white horses differs from the broader category of horses.

name: Potato paradox
description: A counterintuitive percentage puzzle in which potatoes going from 99% to 98% water lose half their total weight.

name: Hedgehog's Dilemma
description: Schopenhauer's metaphor for the tension between seeking human intimacy and avoiding the pain that closeness can cause.

name: Eating your own dog food
description: The practice of an organization using its own products in everyday work to expose flaws and validate the user experience.

name: Girl Late for School with Toast in Her Mouth
description: A supposedly classic shojo manga trope in which a schoolgirl rushes to class eating toast, often colliding with a future love interest.

name: Shaggy God Story
description: A science fiction cliche that rationalizes a biblical myth with futuristic devices, often ending by revealing its characters as Adam and Eve.

name: Ketchup Effect
description: A metaphor for a long delay followed by sudden abundance, named for ketchup that resists flowing until agitation makes it pour out rapidly.

name: Mean World Syndrome
description: A proposed cognitive bias in which sustained exposure to violent media makes people perceive the world as more dangerous than it is.

name: Interesting Number Paradox
description: A humorous self-reference paradox in which the smallest uninteresting natural number becomes interesting simply by being the smallest such number.

name: The Pizza Meter
description: An informal intelligence indicator that treats spikes in late-night pizza orders near US government buildings as signs of an impending crisis or military operation.

name: Banana Equivalent Dose
description: An informal educational unit that compares ionizing radiation exposure with the roughly 0.1 microsieverts associated with eating one average banana.

name: Erdős–Bacon number
description: A person's Erdős–Bacon number is the sum of their Erdős number—which measures the "collaborative distance" in authoring academic papers between that person and Hungarian mathematician Paul Erdős—and their Bacon number—which represents the number of links, through roles in films, by which the person is separated from American actor Kevin Bacon.
